mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its pre-pandemic median for at least 3 consecutive months, long-term discount rates for equities are expected to decline, thereby boosting expected future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day average during similar non-lower-bound periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite a similar labor signal in prior 20-day windows (backtest IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates accelerating economic demand, which typically precedes equity market optimism and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO[12mo moving average] for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 80% of similar INDPRO breakout windows (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which can cause equity risk premia to compress and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by > 0.5% month-over-month AND INDPRO falls by > 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Supply shock or soft landing risk
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive despite repeated CPIAUCSL/INDPRO dual declines in prior windows (IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the 2-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS dynamics) exceeding 3 percentage points in a single month is interpreted as a risk aversion spike, which tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by > 3 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day average during prior high-yield events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in three months while consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) remain above 200,000, it indicates a labor market transition toward full employment, which historically precedes equity market strength and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND UNRATE falls by > 0.1 percentage points over three months AND PAYEMS > 200000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during analogous labor transition episodes (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales proxy (not available in the provided catalog; fallback to HOUST as a demand proxy) below 700 (in thousands) for two months suggests weakening consumer demand, which is associated with elevated equity risk premia and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 700 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative in 70% of similar HOUST decline windows (IC > -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months, despite stable or rising employment (PAYEMS), suggests persistent supply-side frictions that increase uncertainty and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO[12mo moving average] for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS is flat or rising over the same period
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in comparable INDPRO double-dip episodes (IC > -0.1).
